payload.focus: Tanya's sprint retro: async decision widget shipped, 23-point velocity (highest this quarter), Zephyr integration as key unlock
payload.rationale: This sprint retro (dated 2026-09-25) echoes the prior Sprint 4 retro (2026-03-22) almost verbatim — same 23-point velocity, same Zephyr-as-key-unlock claim — so the passes need the prior retro and all its derived positions/observations to detect whether this is a duplicate, an update, or a new sprint confirming earlier claims. I expanded the full narrative chain (DecisionsEvaporate → DecisionCaptureAtConsensus → AntiSlackPositioning) and the core feature position because the async decision widget is the product's primary differentiator and this retro asserts it shipped. I included ContextPreservationNextSprint because this later retro may update or supersede that next-sprint focus. Pricing positions ($12 and $15 tier) and webhook architecture were included because they originate from the same sprint retro document and the passes need them to avoid minting duplicates if pricing or architecture comes up in extraction. I did not expand the People or Documents doors further as they returned no additional axes beyond what the perspective already surfaced.
